short: The United States established the Manhattan Project, a massive secret research and development programme that produced the world's first nuclear weapons.
full:
On 13 August 1942, the United States Army Corps of Engineers established the Manhattan Engineer District to consolidate and rapidly scale up research into nuclear fission. Driven by fears that Nazi Germany was developing a similar weapon, the project grew into an unprecedented industrial and scientific enterprise led by General Leslie R. Groves, with theoretical physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer directing the primary laboratory at Los Alamos, New Mexico. At its peak, the project employed nearly 130,000 people across secret sites in Oak Ridge, Hanford, and Los Alamos.

The project successfully developed two distinct atomic bomb designs: a uranium gun-type weapon and a more complex plutonium implosion device. The culmination of this effort fundamentally altered the course of human history, providing the United States with the destructive capacity to force Japan's surrender without a mainland invasion. The Manhattan Project also laid the technological groundwork for the Cold War nuclear arms race and the subsequent development of civilian nuclear power.
